racecards.race_name: Daily Profit Boosts At betmgm.co.uk Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Gained his Ayr success in the manner of a useful prospect; entered in two Irish Classics
runners.spotlight: 320,000euros breeze-up purchase who justified strong market support at Ayr (7f) in sole 2yo start, scoring in the style of a useful prospect; entered in two Irish Classics; looks well up to defying a 7lb penalty.

runners.comment: 105,000gns yearling; by New Bay; major yard; one of the better types among the newcomers
runners.spotlight: 105,000gns yearling; by New Bay out of unraced half-sister to 1m Group 3 winner Alexios Komnenos; represents major stable and looks one of the better types among the debutants.

runners.comment: 1,000gns yearling; by Mohaather; the least appealing contender among the debutants
runners.spotlight: 1,000gns yearling; by Mohaather out of sprint maiden (RPR 55) who is half-sister to two winning sprinters; the least appealing contender among the newcomers.

runners.comment: Failed to beat a rival at Kempton in sole outing for Alice Haynes
runners.spotlight: Brings the worst form, having failed to beat a rival at Kempton (1m) in sole outing for Alice Haynes; best watched unless the betting suggests a big step forward is likely.

runners.comment: Sibling to three winners, including two for his connections; interesting newcomer
runners.spotlight: Palace Pier colt; sibling to three winners, including two for his connections, notably Native King (7.5f; RPR 94); dam Group-placed 6f 2yo scorer (99); interesting debutant.

runners.comment: Nicely bred; duly showed clear promise in Newcastle maiden; one of the main contenders
runners.spotlight: Nicely bred, being a Kingman half-brother to a Listed winner for his connections and a grandson of Goldikova; duly showed clear promise with running-on third in Newcastle maiden (1m); one of the main contenders.

runners.comment: 75,000gns yearling; by Mehmas; stable had a winning 3yo newcomer ten days ago
runners.spotlight: 75,000gns yearling; by Mehmas out of French/German 1m2f-1m3f scorer (including Group 2; RPR 109); yard had a winning 3yo newcomer (6-5 favourite) ten days ago; heed the market signals.

racecards.verdict: Useful prospect NOBODY KNOWS is taken to follow up his 2yo success, en route to bigger assignments. Sintra should progress.
racecards.betting_forecast: 10/11 Nobody Knows, 7/4 Sintra, 15/2 Mick The Hat, 11/1 Regulus Black, 25/1 The Anthony Gover, 66/1 Mr Maxim, 100/1 My Mate Mackley

racecards.race_name: Always Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Strong at the finish in the second of his two 6f races; likely to stay 7f; leading player
runners.spotlight: Both starts over 6f in October, winning well and strong at the finish in Southwell maiden latest; this colt is likely to stay 7f and holds leading claims despite conceding plenty of weight to the fillies.

runners.comment: Gleneagles half-sister to two winners; sole newcomer in the field; market informative
runners.spotlight: Gleneagles half-sister to two winners, notably War Chant (7f-1m2f including AW; RPR 86); dam sprint maiden (54); sole newcomer in the field; market instructive.

runners.comment: Close fourth at Southwell for new yard, having attracted support; may improve again
runners.spotlight: Never figured in sole start for Alice Haynes but fared a lot better, having attracted support, at Southwell (7f) where she finished a close fourth; may well take another step forward; possibilities.

runners.comment: Kingman filly; showed promise at Newbury in sole 2yo start; entered in Irish 1,000 Guineas
runners.spotlight: Kingman filly who showed promise with third of ten in newcomers' event at Newbury (7f) in sole 2yo start; one of her stable's three entries in the Irish 1,000 Guineas; respected with progress on the cards.

runners.comment: Put in good late work on her way to close fourth of six in C&D maiden; open to improvement
runners.spotlight: Put in good late work on her way to close fourth of six in C&D maiden for an encouraging debut; may be dependent on the cards dropping right if she's again held up in rear; otherwise looks open to improvement.

racecards.verdict: Significant potential is brought by LAHAN KINGMAN. Second choice is Caballo Grande.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/5 Lahan Kingman, 11/4 Caballo Grande, 3/1 Leonie, 7/1 Glasgow Kiss, 50/1 Florizelle

racecards.race_name: Always Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM Handicap (Div I)

runners.comment: Nearly made all in first-time cheekpieces over C&D most recently; good chance
runners.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is proving largely consistent; nearly made all in first-time cheekpieces over C&D most recently and that form has a solid look to it; good chance in the retained headgear with Harry Vigors taking off a useful 7lb.

runners.comment: Remains well treated on best turf form and takes a drop in class
runners.spotlight: Lacks solidity based on his AW record and failed to beat a rival at Wolverhampton (on debut for new yard) most recently; however, remains well treated on best turf form and takes a drop in class.

quotes.race: Graham Lee Vickers.Bet Leger Legends Classified Stakes
quotes.quote: I thought I'd got it. Terries Royale is a nice horse but still so babyish. He travelled nearly too well into the race, hit the front and was just green. He got lonely, it was a shame nobody came to me earlier. It's frustrating but there's plenty of improvement to come in him - Megan Nicholls, jockey.

quotes.race: LK Bennett Lady Amateur Jockeys Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys)
quotes.quote: Terries Royale has taken me into the race, but when he's got there he's been a bit green and wondered what to do. When Becky Smith came on Shaladar he then had something to concentrate on. He was really gutsy. I had to switch but he saw it out well on ground he clearly loves - Serena Brotherton, jockey.

runners.comment: Suited by Wolverhampton; ran respectably last time; possibilities back down in grade
runners.spotlight: Has plenty of Wolverhampton form, notably four wins in Class 6; kept on for respectable third in Class 5 contest here (6f) with reappearance under her belt; possibilities back up in trip and back down in grade.

quotes.race: Join Our Bet Club At Vickers.Bet Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: White Umbrella relaxed well today and I allowed her to find her feet. She quickened nicely and it was quite a nice performance. She did everything right, but it was only the last half-furlong I thought I'd win. I'm sure she'd get a mile, although I'd be happy to see her over seven next time - Kieran Shoemark, jockey.

runners.comment: Clearcut winner in January but nowhere near that form otherwise this year
runners.spotlight: Only 1-16 on AW, the success admittedly gained in clearcut style at Southwell in January; a possible danger on that form but has been nowhere near it otherwise this year; not a solid option.

runners.comment: Revival possible on debut for a trainer who won on him during riding career
runners.spotlight: Out of sorts last year for Martin Dunne but was previously a dual winner for Roger Teal, including under Adam Kirby who has recently commenced his training career and now houses this gelding; interesting off reduced mark dropped in class, with a revival possible.

prev_owners.owner: Sas Logistics Contracts Ltd Nikki Evans

runners.comment: The question is whether his Ffos Las form can be transferred to AW on reappearance
runners.spotlight: Ended his 2025 campaign in good form over the extended 7f at Ffos Las, recording an account-opening win prior to a respectable effort; the question is whether he can transfer the ability to AW on reappearance.

quotes.race: Ken Meredith Memorial Race Handicap
quotes.quote: Sofian promises lots but had delivered nothing until today. I think he wants a mile, but he's probably too weak to get it, so coming back to seven with a bit of cut in the ground has paid off. He always battles hard but I don't think he'll ever win by much; he's just that type of horse - Nikki Evans, trainer.

runners.comment: Still a maiden but has shown signs that he's capable of winning a race of this nature
runners.spotlight: Still a maiden but went down by only a neck at Wolverhampton (8.5f) in December and Kempton (7f) latest start, showing clear signs that he's capable of winning a race of this nature; those are two of his six placed efforts in total; not ruled out.

prev_owners.owner: Making Headway Racing, Cassie And Wilson
Making Headway Racing And K Scott

stable_tour.quote: We got him from the online sales in February. We know the jockey PJ McDonald quite well and he's ridden him previously. He was bad debt in his last yard which is why he was for sale. It's taken us a few runs to get to know him. In his last run, at Ayr last week, he was fifth but it was a very hot race and I really think he's ready to kick on and win in his next few runs. 17-07-25

runners.comment: Ties in with Al Hofzan on the solid piece of form that took his C&D form figures to 123
runners.spotlight: Only 1-25 in handicaps, the win on turf last summer; however, ties in with Al Hofzan on the solid piece of form that took his C&D form figures to 123; enters calculations off same mark kept to this scenario.

stable_tour.quote: He runs in the colours of Constitution Hill's owner Michael Buckley, who was my first ever owner and a very dear friend. Michael is enjoying a good time as an owner not only with the Champion Hurdle winner, but a lovely horse called Florida with William Haggas and I think this is a very nice horse too. He won well at Wolverhampton last time over 7f. He will be ready by mid-April, but as he has only had two runs we will have to carry a penalty in a novice, which is not ideal but it is what it is. We will probably go for 7f again, but he will get further. I think we have a nice horse on our hands. 29-03-23

runners.comment: Form over C&D includes a win last October and an encouraging effort on Friday; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-12 for current yard but his form over this C&D includes sole success, which was gained off 9lb higher last October, and an encouraging effort (finished second) on Friday; fighting chance provided he belies recent inconsistency.

stable_tour.quote: We've loved this horse since we saw him and he's ticked every box twice at home. He's got a big engine and a lot of ability. He made his debut at Chester but wasn't able to show what he's about. He missed the break and got stuck out the back -  it can happen round there. He then went for a Leicester novice where he ran a belter to be denied on the line. I'm seriously considering Royal Ascot for him, either the Windsor Castle or the Norfolk. He's probably more of a 6f horse but I wouldn't be afraid of a stiffer five either. He's got an exceptional mind and is everywhere you need him to be in his work. I think a lot of him. 30-05-24

prev_owners.owner: The Bottom Liners & Mrs R Carr
Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

runners.comment: On a long losing spell and current mark reflects a decline in his form
runners.spotlight: Fairly useful on his day but is on a long losing sequence and current mark reflects a general decline in his form; a regular at Newcastle and rarely seen at Wolverhampton.

stable_tour.quote: We all know what aeat sire Kingman is but not everyone remembers Swiss Lake, who was a two-time Listed winner. Despite hereeding, Swiss Ace still has a lot to prove being without a win since December 2023. Finished mid-division at Redcar on Monday and should progress. 09-04-25

racecards.verdict: With the cheekpieces retained and Harry Vigors taking off a useful 7lb, AL HOFZAN is preferred. Good Karma is second pick.

racecards.race_name: Always Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM Handicap (Div II)

runners.comment: This easier off his last winning mark for a yard among the winners; stamina to prove
runners.spotlight: This easier off his last winning mark for a yard among the winners of late; has only been beyond sprint trips twice during a long career, though, and has stamina to prove.

runners.comment: Boasts a decent record in handicaps round here; excuses latest and goes on the shortlist
runners.spotlight: Boasts a decent record in handicaps round here (two wins and two seconds from six starts) and ran better than his final position suggests over C&D from a wide stall two weeks ago; one to consider.

quotes.race: talkSPORT Powered By Fans Handicap
quotes.quote: Landlordtothestars is a big unit. He's just learned to get himself together, he's so big from his head to his feet. The penny's been dropping a bit and he was in the right company - Dougie Costello, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Pulled hard for new yard over 6f at Southwell last Tuesday and will need to settle better
runners.spotlight: Regressive maiden for Ed Walker who can hang left and was picked up for 5,000gns last month; 40-1, pulled hard in front for her new yard over 6f at Southwell last Tuesday and will need to settle better back up in trip.

runners.comment: Plenty of short-priced defeats for Marco Botti and expensive to follow for this yard too
runners.spotlight: Plenty of short-priced defeats to go with his sole win for Marco Botti and has been similarly expensive to follow for this yard; another switch in headgear didn't help last time (back to blinkers here) and there can only be so many excuses.

runners.comment: Consistent record over C&D down the years and arrives in cracking form; leading claims
runners.spotlight: Consistent record over C&D down the years and arrives in cracking form off the back of a win here on Friday; having the experienced Ryan Kavanagh take off 5lb won't hurt under a penalty and he looks set to go well again.

quotes.race: Best Racing Odds Guaranteed At BetMGM Handicap (Rider Restricted Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Bomb Squad is a superstar and he has been in spectacular form this year. He's run some good races over seven [furlongs] prior to this without winning so we were confident he'd get the trip and, to be fair to Cieren Fallon, he insisted we stepped him up to seven - John Mackie, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Race didn't pan out his way last time but he's looked happiest at Lingfield thus far
runners.spotlight: Race didn't pan out his way last time but he's looked happiest at Lingfield thus far; often misses the break and will need things to set up if dropped in as anticipated from the outside stall.

runners.comment: Lacked consistency in Ireland so may well bounce back from a lesser effort last time
runners.spotlight: Well suited by soft ground; shaped fairly for her new yard over C&D in January and, while she didn't build on that last time, she lacked consistency in Ireland so may well bounce back.

quotes.race: Visit The Irish National Stud & Gardens Maiden
quotes.quote: Pickersgill is a bit opinionated in the parade ring and Robbie said she wasn't doing a tap in front. She got spooked 200 metres from the line at the yellow marker and then she just picked up and went again. She's better than what she showed there as if there is something to bring her further into the race, it would suit her. She had them off the bridle quite early on. She's going the right way and is improving. I don't think soft ground is a must for her but a lot of Starspangledbanners do enjoy a cut - Sheila Lavery, trainer.

runners.comment: New 3lb higher mark has kicked in since a lesser effort from the front over C&D on Friday
runners.spotlight: Useful sprinter in his younger days who's nothing like as good now but remains generally consistent; new 3lb higher mark has kicked in since a lesser effort from the front over C&D on Friday.

quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe has run a cracker. He had a long time off so it's great to see him improve with each run. He seemed to enjoy himself out there today so let's see how he comes out of this. Hopefully we can have a think about Aintree for him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Bowl Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jack (Kennedy, jockey) said he was never happy with Gerri Colombe the whole way, he said he was slack the whole way, but, look, it shows the goods the horse has. He said he probably ended up in front too soon, but he's a great horse. He only does what he has to do. We're lucky to have him. I actually think he'd be a bit better on better ground, but it will be all systems go for the Gold Cup next year. We'll probably go the same route again and keep dreaming - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe ran a great race and we got a lot closer to the winner this time. The loose horse didn't help us but it didn't make the difference between winning and losing. The winner was very, very good - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Savills Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: We've no excuses, everything went even more smoothly for Gerri Colombe than it did at Down Royal. He jumped and travelled great, but the winner just picked up and went away. The winner was unreal. The gallop was strong the whole way and I was happy. The winner just picked up and went away from me - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Champion Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: We were delighted with Gerri Colombe as we knew there would be improvement in him today, his first run in open company. He only came back in on September 19, so there's loads of improvement. We'll have one run now and then the Gold Cup. He showed that he is in the mix now for the Gold Cup, he stays very well and that's what you need. Jack [Kennedy] said he was a bit rusty early, but I thought he was pretty much foot-perfect, apart from one, for a novice stepping into open company. The sky is the limit - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Air Charter Service Mildmay Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were happy the whole way. Gerri Colombe is a good horse. We were disappointed we got beaten at Cheltenham, I think we were the best horse in the race. That proved it today. He's a horse to look forward to for next year. We'll look to the future now, Cheltenham is over. You have to dream in this game and he looks to have a whole lot of potential - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe has been beaten a short-head in a Grade 1 and a stride over the line he is a neck in front, so of course I retain faith in him - he's top class. However, whether he has another run this season is something that will have to be discussed with the owners as he has definitely had a race there - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Scilly Isles Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: If Gordon Ellliott decides he doesn't want to go to Cheltenham (this season) I'd have no issue with that. Next season Gerri Colombe could be a Gold Cup horse. I'm sure there will be ante-post punters going bananas because I've told you he might not go to the festival but we're looking at next year and the Gold Cup for this horse if we can keep him sound. The only thing that has been ruled out today is the National Hunt Chase, because we can't qualify - Brian Acheson, owner.

quotes.race: Guinness Faugheen Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe just keeps winning. He doesn't do anything fancy at home and when he got to the front he pulled himself up again. We're lucky to have him. We'll have a look to see where he might run next - I don't know yet. The National Hunt Chase, or something like that, might suit if the ground was soft. He's a lovely horse who wouldn't like the ground very quick. He was a big baby last season and is coming to himself now - Gordon Elliott, trainer

quotes.race: Irish National Hunt Steeplechase Committee Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe was good I thought. He was having a good blow afterwards and Jack thinks he'll come on for the run. He might go to Limerick at Christmas - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor W.T. O'Grady Memorial Irish EBF Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe won in spite of the track, we ran him here because of the lack of races. He needs more ease in the ground and I imagine he'll go straight to the Albert Bartlett - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: I.N.H. Stallion Owners EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe is still very green for a horse who has done so much. He still has a lot to learn. He jumped well and he's a beautiful horse to look forward to. There's a nice bit of class there and he stays well. He's a nice horse - Denis O'Regan, rider.

quotes.race: Paddy Power (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe is going to be a lovely horse next year for his owners and we're just delighted with that. Next year is the year for him when he goes jumping and anything he does this year is a bonus. He's won two bumpers now and is exciting - Jamie Codd, rider.

quotes.race: Racing Again January 30th (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: I don't think you'll see a whole lot more of Gerri Colombe this season, he might have one more run. He's probably going to be a big chaser more than anything, a big staying horse down the road - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's back cantering away but you won't see him this side of Christmas. It's all going to be baby steps with him and we definitely won't be rushing him. He has no Grade 1 penalty anymore, so that opens up a few easier options for him. Something like the race at Tramore on New Year's Day could be an option. We'll decide closer to the time. Whether he's still a Gold Cup horse or we need to be looking at the Grand National for him, only time will tell. He's been an incredible horse over the years and owes us nothing. 26-10-25

quotes.race: Race And Stay At Leopardstown Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Perceval Legallois was very nimble over hurdles. I thought coming here he's a better chaser than he is a hurdler but he was good there. He's in the Grand National so we'll have to consider it - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Paddy Power Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Perceval Legallois got me out of trouble! It didn't go to plan. I didn't want to be as far back as I was. They kicked on down the back straight and I was a good bit back, further than I wanted to be, but I weaved my way through and he winged the last. I thought coming down to the second-last I had a chance if he kept going the way he was going. I got a great kick out of that because the horse deserved it. He's been unlucky on his last few runs. I knew the ability was there but nothing went right on his last few runs - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: P.J. Foley Memorial INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: That was great from Percival Legallois. We've liked him and I was fairly confident he'd handle conditions. Obviously we were very afraid of Willie's horse coming here but I'm not one bit surprised because he has shown us plenty at home - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He did well last season, winning the Paddy Power at Leopardstown over Christmas and then going back there to win over hurdles at the Dublin Racing Festival. He's been a bit frustrating and the handicapper keeps pushing him up a little bit despite him not winning. He might just not be well handicapped anymore but hopefully he'll have a good chance in one of those staying handicap chases if things fall his way. 13-11-24

quotes.race: Colm Quinn BMW Handicap Chase

It was a great way for him to lose his claim. This fellow has been really running well in beginners' chases where you meet the top novices off level weights. quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle

quotes.race: William Hill Each Way Extra Challenge Series Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Harry's Dream had been placed in bumpers and ran very well in a maiden hurdle, but then disappointed. He ran a good race the last day and I'd say racing down the hill helped today. He struggles on good ground because of his confirmation, and struggles on heavy due to his wind. He'll stay doing what he's doing now - Philip Rothwell, trainer.

runners.comment: Not a bad debut for this stable in a Clonmel claimer and one to consider
runners.spotlight: Won over 2m3f on good ground at Limerick last year off this mark but couldn't cope with higher marks after; not a bad debut for this stable in a Clonmel claimer and one to consider.

runners.comment: Clonmel winner was raised 10lb but could well be progressing enough to defy that
runners.spotlight: Slow burner but has shown improved form since going handicapping and was a decisive winner at Clonmel last time over this trip; raised 10lb but could well be progressing enough to defy that.

quotes.race: Cloneen Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Harty Cup ran well at Gowran when he stayed on nicely on deep ground and needs that ground. While the ground stays like that, he'll stay going in some of those handicaps - Frank Berry, racing manager.

runners.comment: Just denied in a Gowran handicap last time; should run well off 4lb higher for a new yard
runners.spotlight: Maiden was just denied in a Gowran handicap last time when finishing 14l in front of Harty Cup, though that one has improved since; should run well off 4lb higher for a new yard.

runners.comment: Third in a Leopardstown handicap over 2m2f; raised 3lb and this trip should be fine
runners.spotlight: Went closest to scoring when third in a Leopardstown handicap over 2m2f last time on heavy; raised 3lb and this trip should be fine so one to consider.

runners.comment: Beaten 11l by Harty Cup at Clonmel last time on first run for 343 days; fitter now; player
runners.spotlight: Raced a bit fresh when beaten 11l by Harty Cup at Clonmel last time on first run for 343 days; is 10lb better off with that rival and should strip fitter now so can be a player.

runners.comment: Beaten 33l at Naas last time; can do better in this grade but still best watched for now
runners.spotlight: The best of three maiden hurdle runs was when beaten 33l at Naas last time; can do better in this grade but still best watched for now.

runners.comment: Well beaten in three maiden hurdles; do better in this grade though others still preferred
runners.spotlight: Showed ability in points without winning; well beaten in three maiden hurdles but can do better in this grade, though others still preferred.

runners.comment: Well beaten on all hurdle starts for this yard and may need better ground
runners.spotlight: Won a Newmarket novice over 1m for William Haggas in 2024; well beaten on all hurdle starts for this yard and may need better ground.

racecards.verdict: HARTY CUP (nap) improved plenty to score easily at Clonmel and can defy a 10lb rise to win again.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Harty Cup, 4/1 Westoftignes, 5/1 Comanche Moon, 6/1 The Dancen Kid, 13/2 Good Deal, 7/1 Harry's Dream, 14/1 You Done Well, 25/1 Native Policy,  Poppycon,  Kilt, 28/1 Real Petite

racecards.race_name: Michael O'Murchadha Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Good Flat horse and now tackling his first handicap over jumps; has won a maiden
runners.spotlight: Good Flat horse and he won a Galway maiden hurdle in 2024; got competitive some way out when a respectable third at Punchestown last time (heavy); now tackles his first handicap over jumps and firmly in the mix.

quotes.race: Irishinjuredjockeys.com Rated Race
quotes.quote: Jabbar won well. I wondered with the weather would he be fit enough but he clearly was. We won't go back over hurdles until April maybe but we'll stay on the AW until then - Ger O'Leary, trainer.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Tommy Carberry Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I thought it was a good performance. It's a great race to win, because Tommy Carberry was my hero when I was a young fella growing up. One Big Boum looked to be in control and he stretched out well to the line. He's an improving horse and the blinkers certainly make a difference to him. He's effective on that ground and it looks very necessary. He could go to Punchestown but it depends on the ground - Phillip Fenton, trainer.

quotes.race: Ardmulchan Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: First-time blinkers were a big help. One Big Boum is big enough to jump a fence, so I'm sure we will end up over fences maybe sooner rather than later. His jumping was immaculate today, so we are very pleased. He ran at Christmas, so I'm sure it will be three to four weeks before we will ask him to go again - Philip Fenton, trainer.

runners.comment: French winner; long-time absent; market useful on handicap/stable debut
runners.spotlight: Bought for 40,000euros after winnning a French hurdle on very soft in October 2024; absent since but he's an unexposed handicap debutant from a top yard and interesting to gauge any levels of confidence behind him.

runners.comment: Exposed 11yo who is back hurdling over what looks an inadequate trip
runners.spotlight: Should be on a fair mark and there was a return to form over fences at Sandown on his penultimate start (3m); however, he's back hurdling over what looks an inadequate trip.

quotes.race: Cawley Furniture Novice Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Digby toughed it out and is a real stayer. He will jump a fence. We'll see how he comes out of this but I'd say we will go to Punchestown if there is something suitable - Dermot McLoughlin, trainer.

quotes.race: Killarney Plaza Hotel Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Richie said Digby is a grand horse, is still a bit raw and said they went a good gallop. He said he knew from the bottom of the straight he had them covered and he stays going well. Winter ground is an unknown but has been running on quick ground and that's the softest ground he has run on yet. He has been on the go a while but we'll see what the boss man (owner Pat Conway) wants to do. He'll jump fences next year - Dermot McLoughlin, trainer.

runners.comment: Tough task last time at Leopardstown but perhaps a shade high in the weights now
runners.spotlight: Has won three of her last seven races, the latest a small-field novice at Naas; faced a tough task last time at Leopardstown but perhaps a shade high in the weights now (latest handicap victory was off 93).

runners.owner: John T O'Connor & Michael P Gleeson
runners.comment: Not had much racing so a 6lb higher mark than at Naas could still be workable
runners.spotlight: Sat off a strong pace when beating 15 rivals at Naas (1m7f, heavy) but that was his third win over hurdles and this 6lb higher mark could still be workable, as he's not had that much racing.

runners.comment: Rated lower in this discipline but has been below his best over fences the last twice
runners.spotlight: Dual chase winner who is 0-15 over hurdles; rated lower in this discipline but has been below his best over fences the last twice.

runners.comment: Thoroughly exposed five-time winner but has placed form this season
runners.spotlight: Often front runs; thoroughly exposed five-time winner but has placed form this season and could easily run well despite being 3lb wrong at the weights; the visor returns.

quotes.race: Book Your Winter Festival Tickets Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Getting Must Meet Cecil's head in front in the first claimer really helped him and he's enjoying it a lot more now. He was passed up the run-in but battled back, it was a very brave effort. He'll stay going now as long as the ground doesn't get too heavy - Cian Collins, trainer.

quotes.race: Bright Motor Group Claiming Hurdle
quotes.quote: Must Meet Cecil loves good ground and to make plenty of use of him, he's just a big galloper - Cian Collins, trainer.

racecards.verdict: He's got another hefty rise in the weights to deal with but ONE BIG BOUM has looked a different horse in blinkers.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 One Big Boum,  Give Him A Chance, 11/2 Jabbar,  Becasse, 10/1 Tir Og, 14/1 Dont Go Yet, 16/1 Must Meet Cecil, 20/1 Digby

racecards.race_name: William Hill Each Way Extra Challenge Series Beginners Chase

runners.comment: Not a bad chasing debut at Galway (2m2f) in July; has the ability to run well if staying
runners.spotlight: Won a Fairyhouse maiden hurdle over 2m on only start in that sphere last year; ran respectably on chasing debut at Galway (2m2f) in July on only start since; has the ability to run well if staying this trip.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Great Attitude is a fairly smart horse and we were expecting him to run a big race. He's very honest and will have no problem going further - Thomas Cleary, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Handles soft ground and can be a player on chasing debut if staying the trip
runners.spotlight: Won a Kilbeggan bumper on debut in 2024 and got off the mark over hurdles at Cork over 2m4f in October; handles soft ground and can be a player on chasing debut if staying the trip.

runners.comment: Tailed-off on chasing debut at Naas recently so will have to improve hugely on that
runners.spotlight: Triple hurdle winner is rated 120 in that discipline and has won over 3m; however, was tailed-off on chasing debut at Naas recently so will have to improve hugely on that.

quotes.race: Conways Yard "Egg And Spoon" Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Waittillitellyou hasn't really had his ground but he is very effective on that. Hopefully that might get him into Fairyhouse but he will need plenty of juice in the ground - Eddie Cawley, trainer

quotes.race: Meath Farm Machinery Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Waittillitellyou hasn't had that many runs because we had various problems. Coming here today I thought if he didn't run reasonably well we'd be looking for another job for him - Eddie Cawley, trainer.

runners.comment: Runner-up at Gowran over 2m3f; similar ground today; the one to beat if staying this trip
runners.spotlight: Won a Downpatrick maiden hurdle over 2m3f last summer; the best of three chase runs came last time when a 3l runner-up at Gowran over the same trip; similar ground today and is the one to beat if staying this trip.

racecards.verdict: This trip is a question for YORADREAMER but he has the best chase form, courtesy of his Gowran second last time, and can take this.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/5 Yoradreamer, 100/30 Great Attitude, 4/1 Kevin's Pride, 8/1 Waittillitellyou

racecards.race_name: Botanica International Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Last year ended on a low note and again below his best at Leopardstown two weeks ago
runners.spotlight: Is 1-19 over fences; last year ended on a low note and again below his best at Leopardstown two weeks ago; belatedly tries cheekpieces at the age of 11.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes "We Play Together" Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Baldur's Gate got a great spin from James, the horse just needed the 7lb off over the trip. He's just had a few niggly problems but we always thought he was a nice horse, He's a gent of a horse. We'll find something over Christmas - Denise O'Shea, trainer.

runners.comment: C&D winner but beaten between 10l and 14l in his last three races
runners.spotlight: C&D winner last August off 3lb lower but only by the skin of his teeth and has been beaten between 10l and 14l in his last three races; needs to pull out more to win again but should run well.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Finnians Row got a bit of a freebie in front, had a good look at his fences but he was pricking his ears and filling himself up all the time. The owners have stuck by him in fairness. There had been talk of him going to the sales so we will see what happens - Conor Maxwell, rider.

runners.comment: Good run in November but has regressed in each of his subsequent runs
runners.spotlight: Good run over hurdles when back from a break at Navan in November but has regressed in each of his subsequent runs, last time pulling up on his return to fences (0-7).

runners.comment: Struggled over fences last year and again on the Flat since moving yards
runners.spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner in 2024; struggled over fences last year and again on the Flat since moving yards.

runners.comment: Only 4l down when falling at the last on chase debut at Thurles
runners.spotlight: Is 0-8; some promise over hurdles and was only 4l down when falling at the last on chase debut at Thurles; likely to run well if he still fancies the challenge.

runners.comment: Has won four times over fences and his last three efforts have all been positive
runners.spotlight: Has won four times over fences and his last three efforts have all been positive, in the latest finishing ahead of Long Road; has form here and should go well; trip/ground fine.

quotes.race: Racing Again February 20th Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Lake Chad winged the third last and I didn't want to disappoint him and I kept him rolling. He knows his job and he is some servant. He just sees out his races and he was always doing enough to win - Niall Moore, rider

quotes.race: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Lake Chad is better around here than anywhere else. He has won here before and has always run a good race here. He ran terrible the last day and I don't know why he ran so poor. The ground was soft in Roscommon that day. It was a big improvement today - Philip Fenton, trainer.

quotes.race: Waterford Chamber Of Commerce Beginners' Chase
quotes.quote: Lake Chad will maybe get a little break now and come back here for the August meeting - Philip Fenton, trainer.

runners.comment: Back to form when third at Navan in a handicap hurdle; has won over fences
runners.spotlight: Back to form when third at Navan in a handicap hurdle he was placed in the previous year; tailed off and pulled up in his last two chases but has won in this discipline and could have a say.

quotes.race: Overlander Horseboxes Novice Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Chosen Diamond is a horse I didn't think I would be waiting until now to win with. I never lost faith in him. We started schooling him a month ago and I though this was his game. He was very professional and is a natural jumper - Eddie Cawley, trainer

runners.comment: Dual winner over hurdles but hasn't produced an effort of note since late 2024
runners.spotlight: Dual winner over hurdles but hasn't produced an effort of note since late 2024, including over fences on last three runs.

quotes.race: Racing Home For Easter Festival 30th March To 1st April Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Knockbrack Rambler got a great ride from Cal who just waited and waited. The ground was maybe too soft the last day, not as deep today. We might go again in a couple of weeks - Brendan Walsh, trainer.

runners.comment: Outclassed beginners' chases but hard to make a solid case on this handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Completed in one of his four points; has been outclassed in beginners' chases but hard to make a solid case on this handicap debut.

runners.comment: Dual hurdle winner; 0-4 over fences and will need to step up on her 19l defeat last time
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner; only had the four goes over fences and will need to step up on her 19l defeat last time (2m4f).

quotes.race: Ardmulchan Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were very happy coming here today. Eoin knows her so well, he's been schooling her for years and gets her jumping. Butty O Brien was able to dictate and I thought she was impressive. There's a meeting here in about three weeks which we might come back for - Pat Magee, trainer.

quotes.race: Buy Your Navan 2024 Membership Now Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Butty O Brien was very game but she got a class ride from Eoin. She has had little niggly problems but it's great to get off the mark with her today - Pat Magee, trainer

runners.comment: 0-9 over hurdles but now goes chasing with a pointing background
runners.spotlight: Is 0-9 over hurdles but now goes chasing with a pointing background and this could be more his game; still risky.

runners.comment: Beaten 15l in a Thurles handicap but was placed and good to see him get round
runners.spotlight: Consecutive unseats in maiden hunter chases but got round to finish third in a handicap at Thurles (2m5f, soft), albeit some 15l behind the winner; has each-way claims.

runners.comment: This trip might be on the sharp side even if he takes to fences and cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden hurdler; a positive run when a 12l third of 17 at Thurles last month (2m7f, soft) and perhaps heavy ground found him out last time; however, this trip might be on the sharp side even if he takes to fences and cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Fences remain a grey area, as are the new blinkers, and there are trip concerns as well
runners.spotlight: Winning pointer; unseated midrace on her chase debut (3m) but hit the frame (beaten 11l) back over hurdles at Naas when tried in cheekpieces; fences remain a grey area, as are the new blinkers, but probably has a race in her off this mark; may need further.

runners.comment: Sole placing in eight chases was a very remote second at Punchestown in January
runners.spotlight: Sole win came on the Flat in Britain; clearly not bred for fences and his sole placing in eight chases was a very remote second at Punchestown in January; pulled up since then.

quotes.race: More Flat Racing On Racing TV Median Auction Maiden Stakes
quotes.quote: The hill has helped him there, Just For Use really galloped to the line - Joanna Mason, jockey.

runners.comment: No wins in 18, with seven defeats over fences; doesn't look a winner waiting to happen
runners.spotlight: No wins in 18, with seven of those defeats over fences; doesn't look a winner waiting to happen; new yard.

runners.comment: Reserve; mixed fortunes in his four handicaps over hurdles; chase debut here
runners.spotlight: First reserve; mixed fortunes in his four handicaps over hurdles, beaten 11l and 14l on the good days; makes chase debut here.

runners.comment: Reserve; goes chasing as an 18-race maiden hurdler and has ran poorly the last twice
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; goes chasing as an 18-race maiden hurdler and has ran poorly the last twice; there are chasers in the family but best watched.

runners.comment: Reserve; bit of promise over hurdles but now goes chasing after two no-shows
runners.spotlight: Third reserve; not beaten far on handicap debut over hurdles in January but lesser efforts have followed; chase debut.

racecards.verdict: Difficult. The veteran LAKE CHAD has at least produced three solid efforts on the bounce and he rates the safest proposition.

racecards.race_name: Wexfordraces.ie (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race

runners.breeder: M Pascal Beraud & M Bernard Beraud
runners.comment: Point winner has to be respected on bumper debut for a leading yard so check the market
runners.spotlight: Won a Ballysteen point 11 months ago and sold for Eur200,000 after; related to plenty of French jumps winners and has to be respected on bumper debut for a leading yard so check the market.

runners.breeder: M Jean-Pierre Garcon, Mme Isabelle Garcon & M Guillaume Garc
runners.comment: By a leading French sire and commands respect from the Champion trainer
runners.spotlight: Ninth foal; half-brother to winners incl' Thyme White (9.5f 2yo and smart 2m-2m1f hurdle/chase), Meatloaf (bumper and 1m7f/2m3f hurdle) and Joplin (French/German 7f-1m inc AW/Listed; RPR 105); by a leading French sire and commands respect from the Champion trainer.

runners.comment: Disappointing stable debut as 4/5 fav' at Limerick last month and has questions to answer
runners.spotlight: Showed ability without winning in bumpers and maiden hurdles for Kevin O'Donnell; disappointing stable debut as 4/5 fav' at Limerick last month and has questions to answer after that.

runners.comment: Beaten 8l by subsequent Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler at Leopardstown; player
runners.spotlight: A wide-margin winner of a point last year and was sold for Eur350,000 after; promise on bumper debut when beaten 8l by subsequent Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler at Leopardstown; should have improved since and looks a major player.

runners.comment: Runner-up at Fairyhouse in January but was beaten a long way at the same track since
runners.spotlight: The best of four bumper runs was when a close runner-up at Fairyhouse in January but was beaten a long way at the same track since; has questions to answer now.

runners.comment: Solid effort in a Thurles bumper just over a year ago; likely capable of a decent showing
runners.spotlight: Not beaten far in both point starts in 2024; solid effort in a Thurles bumper just over a year ago; an absence to overcome but likely capable of a decent showing.

runners.comment: Beaten 32l on debut at Limerick over Christmas and has to improve hugely on that
runners.spotlight: Beaten 32l on debut at Limerick over Christmas and has to improve hugely on that.

runners.comment: Some ability on first three bumper starts but was tailed-off last time so others preferred
runners.spotlight: Showed some ability on first three bumper starts but was tailed-off at Thurles last time and others much preferred.

runners.comment: Failed to win in five points and well beaten on bumper debut; hood on but can't be fancied
runners.spotlight: Failed to win in five points and well beaten on bumper debut; hood added but can't be fancied.

runners.comment: Nicely-bred but cost only Eur1,000 as a 3yo; respected yard so check market
runners.spotlight: Second foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Jungle Prose (useful bumper and 2m6f-3m hurdle) and Spring Note (bumper and 2m-2m3f hurdle), from the family of high-class 2m-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Oscar Whisky; by the sire of the Gold Cup winner but cost only Eur1,000 as a 3yo; respected yard so check market.

racecards.verdict: Beaten 8l on debut by last week's Cheltenham bumper winner The Mourne Rambler makes a compelling case for MINELLA MACHINE
